name: Zöblen
kurzbeschreibung: Highest village in the Tannheimer Tal, offering a breathtaking Alpenpanorama and excellent air quality.
beschreibung:
Überblick

The municipality of Zöblen lies at 1,087 metres above sea level in the picturesque Tannheimer Tal valley in the Tyrolean district of Reutte (Außerfern), directly beside the Bavarian border. This tranquil mountain village spreads around the confluence of the Vils and Zuger Bach rivers, encircled by striking peaks of the Allgäu Alps including the 1,990-metre Rohnenspitze and the 2,045-metre Ponten. With around 250 residents, Zöblen is the smallest independent municipality in what travel writer Ludwig Steub famously called the most beautiful high valley in Europe. Retaining its authentic alpine spirit, wooden chalet architecture, and genuine hospitality, Zöblen provides an unspoilt retreat for nature enthusiasts and mountain hikers.

Geschichte

Systematic forest clearing and settlement by Alemannic settlers began in the 13th and 14th centuries. The name Zöblen was first recorded in 1399 as Gut Zobel, derived from the homestead of the local Zobl family. Historically governed under the Ehrenberg lordship and the County of Tyrol, valley inhabitants enjoyed ancient privileges regarding salt trade and timber harvesting. To spare villagers the arduous winter journey to church in Tannheim, a local chapel was established in 1682. Between 1791 and 1793, the villagers expanded the building into the late-Baroque Church of St. Joseph, consecrated in 1793. The ornate ceiling frescoes were executed in 1887 by Tyrolean church painter Johann Kärle.

Anreise

Zöblen enjoys excellent, toll-free road access from neighbouring Germany. From the north, the A7 motorway runs past Kempten to exit Oy-Mittelberg or the motorway terminus at Füssen. From there, the route proceeds through Wertach and across the Oberjoch pass on the toll-free Tannheimer federal road B199 straight to Zöblen. From within Austria, drivers travel via the Fern Pass B179 to Weißenbach am Lech and ascend via the Gaicht Pass along the B199. Train passengers arrive at Sonthofen station in Bavaria or Reutte station in Tyrol, with frequent regional buses connecting straight to the village centre.

Tipps

The local peaks Rohnenspitze and Ponten offer rewarding mountain hikes featuring sweeping 360-degree vistas across the Allgäu and Lechtal Alps. In winter, the village's own Rohnenlift serves sunny, family-friendly slopes, directly linked via a ski connection to the Wannenjoch chairlift in neighbouring Schattwald within the Tannheimer Tal ski pass. Cross-country skiers can access the award-winning 140-kilometre valley trail network right from the village, which hosts the famous international Ski-Trail event every winter. For tranquil winter walks, the secluded Zuger Bach valley is ideal, while art lovers will appreciate the historic frescoes in St. Joseph's Church.
